question: Can an app that never uses physics avoid downloading Rapier once @dimforge/rapier3d-compat is installed, and can an app that uses physics later download it only then, without changing any app that uses physics today?
answer: Yes. With aura3d() from @aura3d/assets/vite (physics: 'auto'), the no-physics app emits no Rapier chunk: 6,551,866 B JS (1,927,837 B gzip -9) instead of 9,405,568 B (3,010,601 B gzip), and the browser fetches no Rapier script. With physics: 'lazy' the Rapier chunk is emitted but fetched only on first physics use (2,776 ms after navigation for a scene switched in after 2.5 s), and the physics state after 140 steps is identical. Without the plugin the no-physics app is unchanged against 5.0.2 apart from +4,365 B of engine code (+1,692 B gzip); the physics app built with the plugin is byte-identical to the build without it.

setup.consumer: Clean Vite 8 project (node_modules = npm install of the @aura3d/engine@5.0.2 dependency tree + vite 8 + typescript + @dimforge/rapier3d-compat@0.20.0; the tree from lane 514), @aura3d/engine replaced by the tarball under test. 'absent' = node_modules/@dimforge moved away before the build. Plugin = auraPhysicsPlugin from this branch's packages/assets/dist/vite/auraPhysics.js (what aura3d() adds next to the decoder plugin).

apps.nophys: src/main.ts: createAuraApp with one lit box, no physics (lane 514's consumer app)
apps.phys: phys/main.ts: recipe 16 (docs/agents/recipes-src/physics-basics), physics at startup, ?steps=140 freezes after 140 fixed steps
apps.lazy: lazy/main.ts: recipe 16 scene and calls, but the app starts with a no-physics intro scene and calls app.setScene(physicsScene) after ?delay=2500 ms, then await app.physics.ready()
apps.lazyrecipe: lazyrecipe/main.ts: recipe 16 with one added line, await app.physics.ready(), before its imperative app.physics calls

branch.source: pnpm build && npm pack of lane/519-physics-on-demand

setup.gzip: zlib level 9 over each emitted file
setup.fetch: headless Chrome (real GPU, ANGLE Metal) via loopback CDP; Network.requestWillBeSent over 8-9 s after navigation; networkTimelineMs is relative to the first request (the HTML), appTimelineMs is performance.now() in the page
